title: heap-buffer-overflow in sqlite3Fts5GetVarint
live_proof: backport filter: upstream fix 415540ddaa removes code still present in 3.22.0, and its own regression database reproduces on stock 3.22.0 under host ASan as heap-buffer-overflow in sqlite3Fts5GetVarint
object: the Fts5Data buffer fts5SegIterReverse holds as pLast, measured 2026-10-16: nn=24 bytes, read at iOff=158. The old text, 'the fts5 page buffer the varint decoder reads from', did not say which of the two buffers that function hands to a varint decoder, which is what hid this case's overlap with case 00
lifetime_ender: not a lifetime defect: a corrupt image leaves an offset past the end of the buffer and the varint decoder reads there
shape: read past the end of the record
fidelity: PROPOSED FOR WITHDRAWAL as a duplicate of case 00, not as a case whose trigger misses. Real consumer, real allocator: upstream's own regression image, run statement by statement through the in-domain memfs, and the over-read does happen. But it is case 00's over-read: the same instruction, on the same field of the same structure, in the same 24-byte buffer, differing only in the offset the corrupt image supplies (158 here, 148 there). Measured directly, see PROVENANCE.md

status: no arm re-run on 2026-10-16 and none needed: the case is proposed for withdrawal as a duplicate of case 00, and the evidence is a direct measurement of both candidate lines rather than a re-run (PROVENANCE.md). The earlier readings stand as recorded: spatial run 2026-10-04/05 completes; sublet run 2026-10-04/05 capability fault delivered, cause 5 load out of bounds (spatial) pc=0x1021ba380 -- note cause 5 here against cause 28 on the virtual arm, two different codes for the same over-read across builds; cheribsd-revocation run 2026-10-04/05 completes. One reading in that line is corrected: the probe's kind=UAF is not evidence of a use-after-free. This is a spatial over-read, and the address judgement classifies by WHERE the pointer landed -- an over-read that crosses into a freed neighbour reads as UAF, as the injector's own documentation says -- so kind=UAF means the read left the buffer and landed in a free block, which is a second confirmation of the over-read and not a statement about its class. The arms block below is the 2026-10-11 bundle's; the withdrawal and the single renumber happen when this review ends
note: WITHDRAWAL PROPOSED 2026-10-16, reason: duplicate of case 00. Both cases declare sqlite3Fts5GetVarint as their consumer and both host-ASan stacks are identical to six frames, sqlite3Fts5GetVarint <- fts5SegIterReverse <- fts5SegIterSeekInit <- fts5MultiIterNew <- sqlite3Fts5IndexQuery <- fts5ExprNearInitAll, with identical allocation stacks ending in fts5DataRead. That is not sufficient on its own, because fts5SegIterReverse has TWO unchecked offsets feeding a varint decode and one of them is a MACRO, fts5IndexSkipVarint at sqlite3.c:196291, so a read through it produces no intermediate frame and is indistinguishable in an ASan stack from the decode at :196367. The two read different buffers: the macro reads pLeaf->p, the current leaf, and :196367 reads pLast->p, the page the forward search found. So probe site 60 was written with a hook at each, and both cases were run on one image. Both take the SAME line: case 00 prints SKIPVAR iPoslist=15 nn=22 oob=0 then LASTVAR iOff=148 nn=24 oob=1, and case 25 prints SKIPVAR iPoslist=15 nn=22 oob=0 then LASTVAR iOff=158 nn=24 oob=1. Same instruction, same object, same 24-byte buffer, the other candidate in bounds in both; the only difference is the offset the corrupt image supplies. One limit stated rather than glossed: the two cases cite DIFFERENT upstream commits, adfb203a7d and 415540ddaa, and this environment is offline, so what upstream changed in each cannot be read. Upstream may well have fixed two distinct unchecked offsets, or hardened this function twice; what is measured here is that in the 3.22.0 pin both regression images land on one unguarded read. This corpus counts observables in the pin, so in the pin it is one case. Case 00 is the one kept: it names the buffer (pLast) and the caller, its live_proof quotes the upstream commit message, it was already reviewed and reclassified from temporal to spatial on 2026-10-15 (9061e8fb), and it carries probe site 33 at the same line. No arm is re-run, for case 09's reason: there is nothing here that case 00 does not already measure. Cases 26 and 27 are NOT duplicates of either and were checked the same way: 26 goes sqlite3Fts5GetVarint <- sqlite3Fts5GetVarint32 <- fts5DecodePoslist <- fts5DecodeDoclist <- fts5DecodeFunction, a different path through the fts5_decode debugging function with a different allocator (sqlite3Fts5MallocZero), and 27 is fts3 entirely, sqlite3Fts3GetVarint <- fts3GetDeltaVarint <- fts3PoslistPhraseMerge
fault_sites_why: Host ASan, running the same case source on stock 3.22.0, reports the invalid access in sqlite3Fts5GetVarint (live_proof); that run is independent of the Capstone arms and predates them.
